_comment: TOM'S ALL-CLEARS, one per protected branch, pinned to the commit he cleared.
Keyed and pinned the way dev/english-key-rulings.json is keyed on the exact English text,
and for the same reason: AN APPROVAL MUST LAPSE BY ITSELF WHEN WHAT WAS APPROVED CHANGES.
Clear a branch at one commit, push three more, and 'head' no longer matches -- the gate
closes again without anybody remembering to close it.
WRITE HIS WORDS VERBATIM. 'Yes' and 'Yes, but drop the date validator' are both all-clears
and only one of them is finished. A boolean would lose the difference, which is exactly the
mistake the rulings file already avoids.
AI PROPOSES, TOM APPROVES, THEN AI WRITES -- never AI writing its own permission. If this
file is edited in the same session that merges the branch, and Tom's words are not in the
transcript, the gate has been walked around rather than passed.
